tasks.title: Reload docs match existing behavior and configuration paths serve production callers only
tasks.spec: ## Repository: api; Required behavior R1-R6; Tool facts (cited); Baseline controls C1/C2 and S1-S4; candidate Acceptance 1-9; Security impact checklist and Performance impact. Implement all nine Files paths together: exact R1 paragraph, R2/R3 loader/helper removals with R5 tests migrated to readInitialConfig(nodeConfigFs, path), R4 component-only file edits, and R6 preservation tests. Use the revised literal S4 commands and Acceptance 5's validated-token, readiness and signal-delivery procedure. No README change is needed because runtime behavior, settings, endpoints and README-owned types are unchanged; README.md is protected.

acceptance.expected: Before editing, record the original implementation BASE (planning SHA 515031bd3fd2aa6b8993e325b24ab08f4a3510d6) and Bun 1.4.0. Keep that BASE throughout, not a moving task base. If BASE differs, refresh caller evidence and baseline counts; report a failing baseline test rather than declaring it a mandatory passing control or widening scope to fix it.

S2: on recorded BASE, three runs each print 2 (exit 0); candidate prints 0 (exit 1). Only the unused file-loader chain is removed; readFileSync remains for token readers, and parseConfigText/parseConfig/parseChecks remain live production parsers.

S3: on recorded BASE, three runs each print 8 (exit 0); candidate prints 0 (exit 1). Remove check-only helpers, list selection, replacement/deletion branches and response branch. If retaining a component-only LIST_KEY map as expressly allowed by R4, record that choice and instead run grep -cE 'keepSecret|referenceOf|kind === "check"|case "check"|check: "checks"' src/config-write.ts, with candidate 0 (exit 1); retain the original BASE control count of 8.

acceptance.command:
PULSE_CHECKS_FILE="$T/checks.json" PULSE_DB="$T/pulse.db" PULSE_TOKENS_FILE="$T/tokens.json" PULSE_CHECKS_RELOAD_INTERVAL_MS=1000 PORT=0 bun start > "$T/out.log" 2> "$T/err.log" &
PID=$!
acceptance.expected: Execute the full real-process procedure of Acceptance 5 on candidate HEAD. Before starting: umask 077; create T with mktemp -d and a cleanup trap; use file tools to write the exact valid two-HTTP-check api/web fixture from Acceptance 5 and tokens.json shaped {"tokens":[{"location":"local","token":<fresh random token>}]} using openssl rand -hex 32. Never copy tokens.example.json, use public EXAMPLE_TOKENS or print/report the token; mask 64-hex runs in pasted output. Use interval 1000 (500 is refused), PORT=0 and PID=$! of this launch only. Before any signal, wait at most 10 s in 0.1 s polls for the listening JSON line in out.log; require fileState ok, checks 2, reloadIntervalMs 1000; extract its port and require GET /readyz 200. On process exit or readiness failure, stop and report err.log without tokens; send no signals and do not claim the check. Record GET /metrics ok/invalid/error counters, GET /checks ids and grep -c 'config reload rejected' "$T/err.log" after each step. Literal expectations (ok/invalid/error, rejection lines): 1 initial 0/0/0, 0; 2 kill -HUP "$PID", wait 1 s, 1/0/0, 0 (delivery control; if ok remains 0, stop and report); 3 rewrite api URL to file:///x, wait 2.5 s, 1/1/0, 1; 4 kill -HUP "$PID", wait 1 s, 1/1/0, 1; 5 repeat HUP and wait 1 s, 1/1/0, 1; 6 restore the valid file, wait 2.5 s, 2/1/0, 1; 7 kill -HUP "$PID", wait 1 s, 3/1/0, 1 (second delivery control). Check ids remain ["api","web"] at every step; error remains 0. Stop with kill -TERM "$PID" and wait "$PID": exit 0; pgrep -f "$T" prints nothing, then remove the temp directory. Never signal by name (pidof/pkill). Report actual commands, all seven observations, rejected line (path/message only), readiness, signal-delivery controls and exit/cleanup results without tokens. R1 must agree with steps 3-5's one warning/one invalid count across a poll and two SIGHUPs and step 6's valid apply. These expectations are independently fixed in Acceptance 5 and were verified there three times on BASE, not derived from this candidate run.

acceptance.command:
scope_gate() {
  test -n "$BASE" &&
  test "$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort)" = "$(printf '%s\n' docs/operation.md src/config-reload.ts src/config.ts src/config-write.ts src/config.test.ts src/config.maintenance.test.ts src/config.examples.test.ts src/config-reload.test.ts src/config-admin.test.ts | LC_ALL=C sort)" &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only --cached)" &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only)" &&
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" &&
  git diff --exit-code "$BASE" HEAD -- README.md AGENTS.md src/admin-routes.ts src/main.ts src/start.ts src/config-fs.ts src/config-holder.ts src/check-write.ts src/check-write.security.test.ts src/check-store.ts src/maintenance-write.ts src/metrics.ts src/config-file-state.test.ts src/config-db.test.ts src/config-fs.test.ts src/config-write.audit.test.ts src/config-write.crash.test.ts package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml biome.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js .github bench
}
scope_gate
acceptance.expected: After the task's last commit, gate exits 0: committed paths equal exactly the nine task files; cached diff, worktree diff and porcelain status each empty; protected-path BASE-to-HEAD diff exits 0. Use the original implementation BASE. Also execute this same gate in a disposable fixture repository (not shipped), with the nine allowed files and protected files: clean allowed commit passes; protected worktree-only, index-only and committed edits fail at their respective checks; staged protected edit then worktree restored to BASE fails the index check; committed protected edit then worktree restored to BASE fails the commit check even with base bytes on disk. Allowed uncommitted edits fail; untracked files fail porcelain. Record each of these eight fixture states and the exact check(s) catching it.

Read every added line yourself and list every added comment in the PR body, including inline comments and the rewritten parseConfigText doc comment. Say none only after this complete read finds none. No new test file is in scope; any later approved revision adding one permits at most one explanatory comment line naming the class and expected outcome.

Performance impact evidence: run five interleaved BASE/candidate pairs of this full-suite command on the same shared machine with Bun 1.4.0, matched installs and tracked coverage config; never concurrently. Record user plus system CPU including children, exit status and pass count for all ten runs. Median per side is the third sorted value; report candidate minus BASE to 0.01 s and percent of BASE median to 0.1%. Informational only, no Docker bench or unsupported runtime regression gate.

PR handoff records HEAD and original BASE SHAs, exact nine-file scope and README rationale, C1/C2 and S1-S4 three-run BASE evidence/counts, preservation-on-BASE runs, candidate acceptance 1-8, removed/added test inventory, writer hunk review, real SIGHUP commands/observations/exit status, documentation agreement, security checklist with evidence, all scope/fixture outcomes, complete added-comment inventory and raw CPU samples/medians/delta. No tokens or private details.
